🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-08-31 23:00 → 2026-09-01 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Attribution loop closed at rung 4** — PR #90 advanced through a sequence of structural fixes to recompute attribution under an independent semantic contract, closing an open milestone the group has been working toward. [PR #90](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/pull/90)

> **Profile A gateway independently verified** — A clean recompute at head 59cef8a5 confirmed a full 96/96 test pass, giving reviewers a reliable second signal separate from CI. [tg:tawg:3848]

> **Deployment blocker surfaced before it could land** — Preflight checks confirmed CI and image publication are green but found that production is running a pre-TSEI build, converting a potential surprise into a concrete, named action item. [tg:tawg:3856]

> **VERIFICATION route wiring gap self-caught** — The invinoveritas client was included in the route logic but never connected to the runtime; the gap was identified and reported in the same session it was introduced. [tg:tawg:3935]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### cross-reference-console
_The attribution direction moved through a relay of structural fixes and reached its central milestone._

- Merlini **Closed** the sixth false-green at b1a1344c and resolved a Windows portability issue, removing a persistent source of misleading CI signals that had been making it harder for reviewers to trust the green state. [commit b1a1344c](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/pull/90#issuecomment-5492898857)

- Merlini **Applied** a posture-change fix at 7bf5144 instead of extending an exception list, tightening the CI approach in a way that reduces future maintenance surface and keeps the review signal structurally sound. [commit 7bf5144](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/pull/90#issuecomment-5493066279)

- Merlini **Landed** a capability-set reduction at be8dbed by shrinking scope rather than naming additional exceptions, reflecting the group's preference for structural fixes over incremental allowlist patches. [commit be8dbed](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/pull/90#issuecomment-5493338115)

- Merlini **Completed** rung 4 of PR #90, recomputing attribution under an independent semantic contract and formally closing the attribution loop the group has been working toward across multiple rounds. [PR #90](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/pull/90)

### ccip-router
_The Profile A gateway direction moved to a verified state, with a production deployment blocker now clearly identified._

- Pavlo **Authored** PR #8 adding dedicated gateway operator controls for the Profile A configuration with a required permission check, providing the TSEI implementation the group needs for controlled gateway access. [PR #8](https://github.com/trustless-ai/ccip-router/pull/8)

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Ran** an independent recompute at head 59cef8a5 with a full clean build and all 96 tests matching the PR, giving reviewers a second source of confidence that stands apart from CI. [tg:tawg:3848]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Completed** a deployment preflight that confirmed CI and image publication are clean at the merge commit while surfacing a production-state blocker, turning an ambiguous delay into a scoped, actionable problem. [tg:tawg:3856]

- Merlini (@gobross) **Confirmed** the pre-TSEI production diagnosis, identifying that the profile-a router returns 404s on all paths in the current build, giving the team an exact failure signature to resolve before deploying. [tg:tawg:3895]

- Merlini **Opened** PR #10 to consolidate the CI publisher pipeline with a single publisher, no stale-layer cache, and immutable SHA image tags, strengthening deployment reproducibility for the whole team. [PR #10](https://github.com/trustless-ai/ccip-router/pull/10)

### tawg-daily-contribution
_The VERIFICATION integration and dev-bot tooling both moved forward in the same session._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Documented** the invinoveritas account registration flow, sharing the API endpoint and no-approval creation path so teammates can set up credentials without a manual review step. [tg:tawg:3858]

- Baby Blue Viper **Opened** PR #9 adding the invinoveritas VERIFICATION route with client code, routing logic, and proof confirmation, bringing the integration closer to a testable end-to-end state. [PR #9](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/9)

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Announced** that the dev bot is live on the dev branch with the same codebase as the main bot, giving the team a safe environment to validate changes before they reach the production instance. [tg:tawg:3933]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Self-identified** a wiring gap in PR #9 where the invinoveritas client was present in the route logic but never connected to the runtime, catching a defect that would have caused every verification call to fail silently. [tg:tawg:3935]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- The structural capability-shrinking approach from PR #90 may be worth formalizing as a preferred pattern for other PRs that touch permission scoping
- With the dev bot live, there is now a natural opportunity to validate the VERIFICATION route fix in the dev environment before it reaches the main bot

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Resolve the production pre-TSEI build blocker identified in the ccip-router preflight before deploying Profile A gateway controls
- Wire the invinoveritas client into the runtime to make PR #9's VERIFICATION route functional
- Review and merge cross-reference-console PR #90 now that the rung 4 attribution work is complete

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A preflight, an independent recompute, and a cross-channel confirmation formed a three-step relay that turned a vague deployment risk into a precisely named, scoped blocker — collaborative narrowing at its most useful.
>
> When every link in the chain tightens instead of stretching, even a 404 becomes a gift — keep the relay going! 🚀
